title: NYC Heat Pump Rebates 2026: Con Edison Amounts
desc: New York City heat pump rebates 2026: Con Edison pays up to $11,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed). What stacks and what ended.
h1: New York City Heat Pump Rebates 2026: Con Edison
lead: What New York City homeowners can really get in 2026, checked against Con Edison and NYSERDA on October 3, 2026.
cards_heading: What you can claim in New York City in 2026
cards_intro:
Short answer: In New York City, the main heat pump rebate is NYS Clean Heat (run by Con Edison): up to $11,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home system, taken off your contractor’s bill. It is one rebate, not several that add up. Lower-income households can get much more through EmPower+, and the federal tax credits ended on December 31, 2025.

sections: What makes New York City different

Con Edison supplies electricity across all five boroughs. For gas, Con Edison serves Manhattan, the Bronx and parts of Queens, while National Grid serves Brooklyn, Staten Island and the rest of Queens. That matters because the biggest Clean Heat amounts go to homes that fully replace oil, gas or electric-resistance heat. Many row houses and small multifamily buildings here have old steam or oil systems, which is exactly where a whole-home heat pump pays off most.

Steam heat is the big NYC question. Many pre-war buildings run one-pipe or two-pipe steam boilers, and a heat pump has to replace that heat room by room, often with ductless heads. A contractor who has done brownstone and row-house jobs will size this better than one who mostly installs central systems in the suburbs.

Co-op and condo owners usually need board approval for outdoor units, and some buildings restrict units on the street side. Owners of 1–4 family houses can apply directly. Renters in these buildings may still qualify for EmPower+ even though the landlord owns the heating system.

NYC’s Local Law 97 mostly targets buildings over 25,000 sq ft, so it rarely applies to a one- to four-family home, but it is why some larger co-ops are already planning building-wide electrification.

Clean Heat is the Con Edison rebate, so never add the two together. Clean Heat is capped at 70% of cost (85% in a DAC). There is no separate federal HEAR cheque: New York delivers it through EmPower+. The federal 25C/25D tax credits ended December 31, 2025.

Income-qualified? EmPower+ can cover far more than the utility rebate. Check the state DAC map too: it can raise your amount.
EV chargers in New York City

Con Edison has no rebate for buying a home charger. Its SmartCharge New York program pays about $400 a year on average for charging off-peak. PowerReady stopped taking new Level 2 applications on April 22, 2026.
claim_heading: What to do next in New York City
claim_steps: Find out if your heat is steam, hot water or forced air; it changes which heat pump design fits.
If you are in a co-op or condo, ask the board about rules for outdoor units before you get quotes.
Get 2–3 quotes and ask each contractor to show the rebate tier on the quote.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in New York City?

NYS Clean Heat (run by Con Edison) pays up to $11,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home heat pump in New York City, depending on home size, whether you remove the old system, and DAC status.
Can I get the Con Edison rebate if I live in a co-op or condo?

Individual apartment owners can qualify at the apartment amounts, but you will usually need your board to approve the outdoor unit. Whole-building projects in larger buildings go through Con Edison's multifamily program instead.
Is the federal tax credit still available for heat pumps?
No. The federal 25C and 25D credits ended for anything installed after December 31, 2025.

Lower-income owners and renters of 1-4 family homes. Low-income households can get free upgrades up to $12,000 upstate or $14,000 downstate; moderate-income households get 50% covered up to $6,000 upstate or $7,000 downstate.
